Thanks Camila / Claire — quick finance summary so everyone is aligned: 

1) Contracting vs billing entity: Redwood invoices the contracting entity listed on the Order Form by default. We can accommodate consolidated billing to a parent entity only if:
   - The payer (parent) is the contracting party on the Order Form OR
   - The payer signs a billing addendum acknowledging responsibility for all invoices and referencing the Order Form (simple amendment is fine).

2) Net terms: our standard is Net 30. Net 45 can be approved for named accounts following credit review. Net 60 requires stronger credit review and (in practice) either an upfront partial payment or an approved credit limit — we can discuss but it will add time to procurement.

3) Invoice format: we can produce a consolidated monthly invoice/statement showing per-entity usage lines, which helps reconciliation. If you prefer per-entity invoices, we can do that too — but consolidated payer + per-entity detail requires the mapping in the billing addendum.

4) Taxes: for EU customers with valid VAT IDs, we apply reverse-charge. We require the VAT ID and an electronically signed certificate on file before applying reverse-charge.

Action items:
- Claire: please confirm whether GlacialTech Holdings Ltd will sign as the payer or whether you want the local entity on the Order Form with the parent as payer via addendum.
- Camila: once Claire confirms, I can work up an invoice example and outline the credit checks for Net 45. I’ve attached our credit criteria doc for reference (Redwood_credit_criteria.pdf).

Ben Carter
Head of Finance, Redwood Inference
